A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Φ-ROM research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support a complete comparison, including matching v1 Appendix G to v2 Appendix H.

before.justification: v1 reports original PDE forecasting experiments, baseline comparisons, sparse-observation evaluations, and seed statistics in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experimental results and adds a Burgers’ loss-weight sensitivity experiment in Appendix G.

M1.justification: The decoder, dynamics network, solver-derived targets, loss functions, hyper-reduction, and training/inference algorithms are unchanged. Appendix G studies the existing loss weight rather than introducing a method component.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Diffusion, Burgers’, Navier–Stokes, KdV, and cylinder-flow LBM with the same forecasting and sparse-observation coverage. The new sensitivity study uses the existing Burgers’ task; 3D and time-independent PDEs remain future work.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains DINo, PINN-ROM, FD-CROM, AD-CROM, and subsampled AD-CROM. Tables 2–3 retain the DINo comparison. Expanded discussion of CROM does not add or remove an evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: Appendix G.1 introduces a Burgers’ experiment varying λ across 0.1, 0.5, and 0.9. Existing benchmark splits, grids, architectures, and training budgets remain unchanged. LBM’s λ = 0.8 was already specified in v1 Table 6.

E4.justification: New Appendix G.1 and Table 7 test sensitivity to the reconstruction/dynamics loss balance, reporting both losses and forecasting errors. This adds a focused hyperparameter analysis; existing data-efficiency, sparse-observation, and long-horizon analyses are retained.

E5.justification: The same three matched random initializations and RNMSE means and standard deviations for Navier–Stokes appear in v1 Table 9 and v2 Table 10. The new λ study introduces no additional uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: v2 Table 7 adds Burgers’ error pairs of 0.137/0.150 for λ = 0.9 and 0.459/0.613 for λ = 0.1, plus loss values. The λ = 0.5 errors remain 0.021/0.028, matching the original Table 1. Existing benchmark and seed-statistics results are unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, loss equations, Jacobian projection, QR derivation, and PDE formulations are retained. The added loss-weight discussion and discretization rationale introduce no formal derivation, theorem, or proof.

C1.justification: The conclusion adds an explicit assertion that adherence to convergent solver discretizations makes Φ-ROM robust to physical phenomena relative to other physics-informed approaches. The abstract and five headline contributions otherwise retain their scientific scope.

C2.justification: Appendix G explains how extreme λ values impair reconstruction or dynamics learning and links LBM sensitivity to cylinder-reconstruction artifacts. The conclusion newly identifies dynamics-loss scalability for large 3D problems and extension to time-independent PDEs as unresolved.

D1.justification: The abstract adds an explicit project URL for the advertised JAX implementation. Appendix G supplies additional guidance and rationale for the existing λ choices, including LBM. Hardware, training times, and implementation details otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Appendix A expands the existing CROM comparison with discussion of interpretability and gradient errors that can require full-grid evolution. The cited-work set is unchanged; the updated publication details for reference 41 do not constitute a new citation.

P1.justification: v2 locally expands related work and the conclusion, inserts the loss-weight appendix, and relabels the existing extended-results appendix from G to H. It also updates the publication footer and makes small wording corrections; the main narrative structure remains intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds the λ-analysis Table 7 and renumbers the existing appendix tables accordingly. References, Algorithm 1, and surrounding appendix material reflow. Existing figures and result displays retain their substantive content.

improvement.justification: The new Burgers’ ablation provides direct evidence for a previously stated loss-weight choice, while the LBM explanation and more specific scalability limitations improve transparency. The implementation link also improves discoverability. These gains are limited to focused validation and documentation; the principal method and comparative evidence remain unchanged.
